name: Roberto Rocca
notes: Roberto Rocca, longtime head of Argentina's Techint group and first chairman of Tenaris, died in Milan on 10 June 2003 aged 81 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Rocca). The group is now led by his son Paolo Rocca.

name: Carl Ray Pohlad
notes: Carl Pohlad, Minnesota financier and Minnesota Twins owner from 1984, died 5 January 2009 aged 93 (source: https://www.mprnews.org/story/2009/01/05/pohlad1). The family business continues as Pohlad Companies.

name: Andreas E.Rihs
notes: Andy Rihs, co-founder and longtime CEO/chairman of Phonak/Sonova and backer of the BMC cycling team, died 18 April 2018 aged 75 (source: https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/cycling-supporter_swiss-entrepreneur-and-bmc-cycling-backer-andy-rihs-has-died/44058924).

name: Ryuji Arai
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder, Bic Camera Inc. (Tokyo)
profile: Ryuji Arai founded Bic Camera, the Japanese electronics and appliance retail chain. It began in 1968 as a photo-processing business in Takasaki, Gunma, became Bic Color, and was renamed Bic Camera in 1978, with its first store in Ikebukuro. It listed in 2006 and posted over $6B in revenue in FY Aug 2025. Arai also holds stakes in Hit Communications and contact-lens maker Seed.
interesting_fact: Bic Camera owns a majority stake in the listed satellite TV network Nippon BS Broadcasting (BS11).
deep_cut_fact: Arai's first venture, started in his early twenties, was Takasaki DP Center, a film developing and printing shop in Gunma. Bic Camera grew out of that shop's camera-sales department, which was spun off as Bic Color in 1972.
notes: Very reclusive and gives essentially no interviews (Bic Camera declined to make him available to Bloomberg in 2018). Best route is Bic Camera's PR/IR department via its IR site. A 2009 government press file listed the address kouhou@biccamera.com for PR/IR, but it is old and unverified, so it is not included. He is known as an anti-nuclear advocate: Bic Camera hung banners in 1995 protesting French nuclear tests (https://macaudailytimes.com.mo/?p=91929).

name: Stefania Triva
current_role: President & CEO and largest shareholder, Copan Italia S.p.A. (Brescia)
profile: Stefania Triva runs Copan, the family firm her father Giorgio founded in 1979. Her late brother Daniele invented the flocked swab there in 2003, and Copan is now one of the world's largest makers of diagnostic swabs, along with lab-automation machines and software. She became CEO in 2014 and steered the company through the Covid surge in demand. She holds about 48% and has rejected buyout and IPO offers.
interesting_fact: Flocked swabs made up more than 80% of Copan's $445M revenue in 2021. The Covid-19 testing boom made Triva a billionaire.
deep_cut_fact: In 2023 President Mattarella named her a Cavaliere del Lavoro (Knight of Labour) for the medical-devices industry. She started out as a teenager in the 1980s packing boxes at her father's company.
notes: info@copangroup.com is Copan's general address, published in a 2020 press statement signed by Triva. Copan is private and keeps a low profile; the best route is the corporate contacts page. Copan is now based in Brescia. The box-packing detail comes from a Forbes profile reprinted in Forbes Middle East ('Nose for Business', 2022).

name: David Capobianco
current_role: CEO & Managing Partner, Five Point Infrastructure (formerly Five Point Energy); Chairman of LandBridge (NYSE: LB) and PowerBridge
profile: Houston-based infrastructure investor who founded Five Point Energy in 2012, after co-founding the private equity group at Paul Allen's Vulcan Capital. Five Point built Permian water business WaterBridge and land platform LandBridge (IPO 2024), which own 270k+ acres. Its new PowerBridge unit is developing gigawatt-scale powered data-center campuses, including a 2 GW campus in Reeves County, TX.
interesting_fact: He pitches the Permian Basin as a rival to Northern Virginia as a data-center hub, citing its land, cheap gas, fiber, and produced water for cooling. He has argued that nuclear power, possibly small modular reactors sited at data centers, is the only route to fully renewable data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Vulcan he worked in Salomon Brothers' Energy Corporate Finance Group and on the investment teams of Harvest Partners and Greenhill Capital Partners. He later chaired Vulcan Energy Corp. (formerly Plains Resources) and chaired the compensation committee of Plains All American Pipeline. Duke BA, Harvard MBA.
notes: A strong fit for an energy and data-center podcast: he has spoken on the Cool Vector podcast/Substack and speaks publicly about the Permian, powered land and data centers. For media, go through Kekst CNC (LandBridge's PR firm) or the LandBridge IR address. The Kekst address appeared in older releases, so check that it is still current.

name: Peng Qian
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Wuhan Jingce Electronic Group (300567.SZ)
profile: Peng Qian, born 1974, founded Wuhan Jingce Electronic in 2006 at 32. It started in flat-panel display testing equipment and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2016. Jingce has since expanded into semiconductor metrology and new-energy (battery) testing equipment. Peng remains controlling shareholder, chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: Before founding Jingce he worked in market sales at Guangzhou ASPEC Environmental Instruments, an environmental testing equipment maker. He then built one of China's leading display-inspection equipment makers.
deep_cut_fact: He studied refrigeration equipment and cryogenic technology at Huazhong University of Science and Technology (then 华中理工大学) before moving into instrument sales. He started Jingce in Wuhan in April 2006 at age 32.
notes: Best route is via the company board secretary (董事会秘书 Liu Binghua, per 2026 IR activity records) or the Shenzhen exchange's 互动易 investor Q&A platform. The university/major detail was summarised by search from 36Kr and was not visible on the fetched page, so verify before use. Relevant to semiconductor/new-energy equipment themes.

name: Chen Jianming
profile: Listed by Hurun (2007-2021) and Forbes (2018) as a property developer whose wealth comes from 'Guangda', shared with Chen Runguang. Several searches in English and Chinese (陈建铭 / 陈润广 / 光大) did not establish which 'Guangda' company this is; it is not the state-owned China Everbright (光大) Group.
notes: Identity not confirmed: Chen Jianming is a common name and Guangda (光大) is a common company name. Needs a lookup of the Hurun China Rich List entry (e.g. the 2019 list) to pin down the company and city before any outreach.

name: Lai Miao
profile: Listed on the Hurun China and Global lists (2021-2026) with wealth from Ganten (景田), the Shenzhen bottled-water company behind the Baisuishan (百岁山) mineral-water brand, founded in 1992. Searches did not find public material naming 赖苗 or describing their role at Ganten.
interesting_fact: Ganten's Baisuishan leads China's natural mineral water category, and Hurun valued Ganten at RMB 26B in 2025, top-three among Chinese bottled-water companies.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or bios found. Their role (founder, co-owner or family shareholder) is unconfirmed. Ganten is private, so the only route is likely the company's corporate channels.

name: Li Xiaolai
current_role: Bitcoin investor and author; founder of Bitfund (BitFund.pe) and INBlockchain
profile: Li Xiaolai is an early Chinese bitcoin investor. A former New Oriental English test-prep teacher (2001-2008), he began buying bitcoin in 2011 and founded the crypto venture firm Bitfund in 2013, and was often called 'China's richest bitcoin billionaire'. In 2018 he said he would stop investing in crypto projects. He now writes and publishes, including the book 'The Self-Cultivation of Leeks' (韭菜的自我修养).
interesting_fact: In July 2017 he raised a $200M ICO in China, two months before Beijing banned ICOs. He has publicly disputed the 'richest bitcoin holder' label, writing that he knew others who held more.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he was a bestselling self-improvement author: his book on time management, 'Take Time As a Friend' (把时间当作朋友), predates his bitcoin fame. At New Oriental he received stock options in 2005, an episode he describes as the start of his investing.
notes: Active online and writes in public; his X account and personal site are the most direct routes, and he also lists a WeChat public account. Avoid referencing the 2018 leaked-audio controversy. Only appeared on Hurun in 2018, so his current wealth is unclear.

name: Sergey Shnayder
current_role: Co-founder and co-owner, Svetofor Group (Svetofor/Mayak hard-discount supermarkets; operating companies 'Torgservis')
profile: Siberian entrepreneur (also spelled Schneider/Shnaider) who co-founded Svetofor with his brother Andrei in 2009. The chain is modelled on Aldi, Lidl and Walmart: bare-bones warehouse stores priced at least 20% below rivals. It has grown to over 2,000 stores in Russia and abroad. He started in the 1990s distributing beer and low-alcohol drinks, then ran a beer-store chain from 2004.
interesting_fact: Svetofor deliberately opens stores in run-down suburbs that rivals avoid and buys stock close to its expiry date. It became Russia's fastest-growing supermarket chain and expanded into Germany, the Baltics, Poland and Serbia.
deep_cut_fact: Before discount groceries, Shnayder was a 1990s beer and low-alcohol drinks distributor; in 2004 he and partners launched a chain of stores selling mainly beer, the precursor to Svetofor.
notes: Extremely secretive: the brothers never give interviews and ignore approaches made through intermediaries (The Bell). OpenSanctions lists him on a Lithuanian (LTFIU) sanctions list, so check legal and reputational risk before any outreach. No published contact found. Low relevance to energy/data centers.

name: Yang Xuegang
current_role: Chairman, Executive Director & CEO, China Risun Group (1907.HK)
profile: Yang Xuegang founded Xingtai Risun Coking in Hebei in 1995 and built it into China Risun Group, China's largest independent coke producer. Risun is also a major coke-based chemicals maker, listed in Hong Kong, and is expanding into hydrogen/new energy and new materials. He has been chairman since 1996 and led industry bodies including as president of the Hebei coking industry association.
interesting_fact: Frost & Sullivan ranked Risun the world's largest independent coke producer and supplier by volume in 2020. Its production bases include Xingtai, Dingzhou, Laoting and Cangzhou.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a hydraulic engineer (Hebei Hydraulic College, 1985) and spent about 10 years at Handan's Dongwushi Reservoir Management Center, becoming deputy director in 1988. He still keeps a water link as a director of Beijing Automic, a water-conservancy IT firm.
notes: Relevant to the energy theme: Risun produces hydrogen from coke-oven gas and is pursuing new-energy materials. The best route is Risun IR. Bio details come from the 2025 annual report (published April 2026).

name: Anant Asavabhokin
current_role: Founder and major shareholder, Land and Houses PCL (SET: LH); chairman of Home Product Center (HomePro)
profile: Anant Asavabhokhin (also spelled Asavabhokin) is a Thai property tycoon who co-founded Land and Houses with his mother, Piangjai Harnpanij, in 1983. The company listed on the SET in 1991, is known for detached and semi-detached housing, and has expanded into rental property, including US hotels such as a SpringHill Suites in California bought for $31M in 2021. His family is the largest LH shareholder and he chairs home-improvement retailer HomePro.
interesting_fact: Land and Houses' 2026 plan targets about THB 9.9B in rental property revenue alongside its housing business. The next generation, including Managing Director Achawin Asavabhokhin, now presents the plans.
deep_cut_fact: Besides Thai degrees from Chulalongkorn (undergraduate) and Thammasat (MBA), he holds a graduate degree from the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago. Tatler Asia named him to its 2023 'Asia's Most Influential' list for Thailand.
notes: He stepped down as LH chairman in 2017, when he faced money-laundering charges that he denied (Forbes); avoid this topic. Sources disagree on whether he formally holds an LH board role now. Best route is LH investor relations or HomePro corporate channels. In the interesting_fact, the THB '99 billion' in the source URL slug reads as THB 9.9B; verify the figure.

name: Mahmud Kamani
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Vice Chair, Debenhams Group plc (formerly boohoo group)
profile: Manchester entrepreneur who co-founded online fashion retailer boohoo with Carol Kane in 2006. He floated it in 2014 and built a group including PrettyLittleThing, Nasty Gal and the Debenhams, Dorothy Perkins, Wallis and Burton brands. The group was renamed Debenhams Group; in February 2026 he moved from executive chair to executive vice chair and put £8M into a £40M fundraise.
interesting_fact: His father Abdullah, a Gujarati-heritage Kenyan who moved to north-west England in the 1960s, started out selling handbags on a market stall. He then built a textile business supplying New Look and Primark, which became the springboard for boohoo.
deep_cut_fact: He supports Kibera Kids, a Nairobi-based non-profit, a link back to his family's years in Kenya. He was Entrepreneur of the Year at the 2013 English Asian Business Awards.
notes: The group is in a turnaround and there is ongoing shareholder pressure from Frasers Group, so outreach is best kept to his entrepreneurial story. Go through the in-house press office or its agencies (Threesixty, Sodali). Little energy/data-center relevance.

name: Robert Greenberg
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Skechers (Manhattan Beach, CA; taken private by 3G Capital in Sept 2025)
profile: Serial footwear entrepreneur who founded LA Gear in 1983, then started Skechers in 1992 with grunge-era utility boots. He built Skechers into a top global footwear brand; the company now calls itself the No. 2 footwear brand in the US. In 2025 he agreed to sell Skechers to 3G Capital in a take-private completed in September 2025, and his son Michael is president.
interesting_fact: Before Skechers he built LA Gear into a 1980s sneaker phenomenon, founding it in 1983. He left as CEO in 1992, the same year he launched Skechers.
deep_cut_fact: The family's annual Skechers Pier to Pier Friendship Walk has raised $35M for kids. It funds the $70M Friendship Campus (The Greenberg Family/Skechers Center) for neurodivergent young adults in the South Bay, due to open 21 January 2027.
notes: Hurun lists him with no country (he is US-based). His exact title after the 3G deal was not confirmed from a primary source. The Friendship Walk and Friendship Campus are the warmest openers. Web search budget ran out during this lane, so his early (pre-LA Gear) career was not researched.
